_about: One instant, many clocks. A day read from git is the reader's LOCAL day: git's %at (seconds since the epoch) converted in the reader's zone -- never %ai's date, which is the author's. Read by Tests/Test-BackfillStamps.ps1 and Tests/test_clock.py; both halves must agree on every row. A row is a day the git instant must give in that zone, whatever the host's own clock says.
rows: 23:30 Pacific: the UTC date is already tomorrow
06:30 in Sydney: east of UTC runs ahead
the last second of the year in Pacific standard time
